newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says talks or chaos for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France says talks or chaos for Zaire.

text.p: France said on Wednesday rebels who have seized almost half of Zaire would be responsible for plunging the country into total chaos if they refused to negotiate a democratic settlement.

The foreign ministry said talks between the government of President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila were "the only way out of the current crisis that risks lastingly upsetting balance throughout central Africa".

"Any other way, particularly the conquest of power by force of arms, would drag Zaire into an undefinable chaos, worsening a humanitarian disaster and making the indispensable national reconciliation a more remote prospect," it said in a statement.
"Those who would keep on this path, or accept it, would bear a heavy responsibility towards Zaire and the whole of the region," it said.

France recently distanced itself from Mobutu whom it has supported during most of his 32-year-long autocratic rule. As Kabila's men advanced through Zaire, Paris reluctantly dropped the term "rebels" and started referring to them by their chosen name of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire.
Kabila reiterated on Wednesday that nothing would halt his drive to unseat Mobutu but there were signs that he could soon meet his foe.
Zairean Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba told a news conference in Kinshasa that Mobutu and Kabila could meet directly once their envoys had consulted.

A senior South African source said President Nelson Mandela, who met Kabila on Wednesday, wanted to bring Mobutu and Kabila together in South Africa as part of his efforts to end the civil war in Zaire.
